Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-454", "title": "Viral Infections", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "They are made of genetic material (either DNA or RNA) inside of a protein coating."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "There are a huge number of viruses on earth."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Only a small number of them can infect humans."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Those viruses can infect our cells, which may cause disease."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some of the diseases that viruses can cause include the common cold , the flu , COVID-19 , and HIV ."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Viruses can be spread in different ways: Through droplets and particles that are breathed out by someone who has the infection."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "You might breathe in the droplets or particles, or they could land on your mouth, nose, or eyes."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "By touching surfaces or objects that have the virus on them and then touching your mouth, nose, or eyes."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "From the pregnant parent to the baby during pregnancy ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "By being bitten by an infected insect or animal."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Through sexual contact (usually vaginal, anal and oral sex) with someone who has the infection."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "They then use those cells to multiply (make copies of themselves)."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "This process is also called replication."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "The process can kill, damage, or change the infected cells."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The symptoms can range from mild to very severe."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Other times, your immune system may be able to fight it off and you may not have any symptoms."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Each different virus usually only infects one type of cell in your body."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "For example, hepatitis viruses affect the cells in the liver."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "HIV infects a certain type of immune system cell."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "What are the treatments for viral infections?"}, {"id": "S020", "text": "For most viral infections, treatments can only help with symptoms while you wait for your immune system to fight off the virus."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "There are antiviral medicines to treat some viral infections."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Antibiotics do not work for viral infections."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Vaccines can help prevent you from getting many viral diseases."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "You may be able to prevent some viral infections by: Proper hand washing ."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Cleaning surfaces that may be infected with germs."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Preventing insect bites by using insect repellent when you go outdoors."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "If you travel to an area that has a high risk of diseases from insect bites, also wear long pants, shirts, and socks."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Practicing safe sex (using a condom every time you have anal, vaginal, or oral sex)."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Avoiding close contact with people who are sick."}]}, {"id": "MLP-139", "title": "Anemia", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "If you have anemia, your blood does not carry enough oxygen to the rest of your body."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The most common cause of anemia is not having enough iron ."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your body needs iron to make hemoglobin."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein that gives the red color to blood."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Anemia has three main causes: blood loss, lack of red blood cell production, and high rates of red blood cell destruction."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Conditions that may lead to anemia include: Heavy periods Pregnancy Ulcers Colon polyps or colon cancer Inherited disorders A diet that does not have enough iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 Blood disorders such as sickle cell anemia and thalassemia , or cancer Aplastic anemia , a condition that can be inherited or acquired G6PD deficiency , a metabolic disorder Anemia can make you feel tired, cold, dizzy, and irritable."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "You may be short of breath or have a headache."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Your doctor will diagnose anemia with a physical exam and blood tests."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Treatment depends on the kind of anemia you have."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-5858", "title": "Chest Injuries and Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "The chest is the part of your body between your neck and your abdomen (belly)."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The medical term for your chest is thorax."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your chest holds many important structures for breathing, digestion, blood circulation, and other important body functions."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "These structures include your: Ribs and breastbone Esophagus, the tube between your mouth and stomach Trachea, your windpipe Bronchi, the tubes that carry air from your windpipe to your lungs Lungs Pleura, a thin layer of tissue that covers the lungs and lines the inside wall of the chest space Heart and large blood vessels Thymus, a gland that's part of your immune system Nerves What are chest injuries and disorders?"}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Chest injuries and disorders are problems that affect any of the organs or structures located in your chest."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "There are many types of chest injuries and disorders, for example: Broken ribs Esophagus disorders Swallowing disorders , also called dysphagia Tracheal disorders Bronchial disorders Lung diseases and collapsed lung Pleural disorders Heart diseases Mediastinal diseases, which are tumors, inflammation, and other problems with the structures in the mediastinum, which is the space between your lungs, breastbone, and spine Thoracic aortic aneurysm Thoracic outlet syndrome Chest injuries may happen from the force of car accidents, falls , or sports injuries ."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Or the chest may be pierced by a bullet or sharp object."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Because your chest holds so many important structures, certain chest injuries may be life-threatening."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "How are chest injuries and disorders diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Diagnosis of chest injuries or disorders depends on the type of symptoms you're having and whether you've had a chest injury."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Injuries are usually obvious, but in most cases, you'll need tests to know how serious an injury is."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "There are many types of tests for diagnosing different types of chest injuries and disorders, for example: Diagnostic imaging tests Heart tests Lung function tests Bronchoscopy Pleural fluid analysis Dysphagia tests Biopsy Treatments will depend on the type of chest injury or disorder you have."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1377", "title": "West Nile Virus", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "West Nile virus (WNV) is an infectious disease."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is most often spread by the bite of an infected mosquito."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Most people have no symptoms, while some may develop mild symptoms."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "But WNV can sometimes cause serious symptoms if the virus enters your brain."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "WNV usually spreads to people through the bite of an infected mosquito."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "However, in rare cases, it can spread from person-to-person."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "This can happen through an organ transplant or blood transfusion ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "If you are preganant you can spread WNV to your fetus during pregnancy or delivery."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "And after delivery, it can spread to the baby during breastfeeding ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Who is more likely to develop West Nile Virus?"}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Anyone could be bitten by an infected mosquito and get WNV."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "But certain people are at higher risk for more serious illness they get a WNV infection."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "They include people who: Are over age 60 Have certain medical conditions, such as cancer, diabetes , high blood pressure , or kidney disease Had an organ transplant What are the symptoms of West Nile Virus?"}, {"id": "S013", "text": "But most people have no symptoms or mild symptoms."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Mild symptoms of WNV can include: Fever Headache Body aches Vomiting Diarrhea Skin rash These symptoms usually go away on their own within a few days to several weeks."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "But some people will have weakness or fatigue that lasts for weeks or months."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Although rare, If West Nile virus enters your brain, it can be life-threatening."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "It may cause inflammation of the brain ( encephalitis ) or inflammation of the tissue that surrounds the brain and spinal cord ( meningitis )."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Serious symptoms of WNV can include: High fever Headache Neck stiffness Numbness Coma Muscle weakness Vision loss How is West Nile Virus diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "To find out if you have WNV, your health care provider: Will do a physical exam Will take your medical history, including asking about your symptoms May order blood tests What are the treatments for West Nile Virus?"}, {"id": "S020", "text": "There are no specific vaccines or treatments for human WNV disease."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "But rest, fluids, and over-the-counter pain medicines may relieve some symptoms."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "You may need to be hospitalized if you have serious symptoms."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "There are no vaccines or medicines to prevent WNV."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "The best way to avoid WNV is to help prevent mosquito bites : Wear insect repellent with DEET or another U.S."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)-registered insect repellent."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Make sure to follow the instructions for using the repellent."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Wear long-sleeved shirts and pants if you're outside."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Get rid of mosquito breeding sites by emptying standing water from flowerpots, buckets, or barrels."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Stay indoors between dusk and dawn, when mosquitoes are most active."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Use screens on windows to keep mosquitoes out."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)"}]}, {"id": "MLP-4491", "title": "Moles", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "They happen when pigment cells in the skin, called melanocytes, grow in clusters."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Most people have between 10 and 40 moles."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "A person may develop new moles from time to time, usually until about age 40."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "In older people, they tend to fade away."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "They are usually round or oval and no larger than a pencil eraser."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "About one out of every ten people has at least one unusual (or atypical) mole that looks different from an ordinary mole."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "They may be more likely than ordinary moles to develop into melanoma , a type of skin cancer."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "You should have a health care professional check your moles if they look unusual, grow larger, change in color or outline, or in any other way."}]}]
